$doc: Case body's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component case-body` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/case-body.tsx. Same contract as components/button/definition.json: a plain string is a structural literal, {"token": "x"} binds --x, and an array is a sequence of both. CASE-BODY IS THE BLOCK WITH NO `base`. Its root is a scope, not an appearance — `.case-body` has never had a rule of its own, and inventing an empty one so the schema could stay strict would have recorded a shape the stylesheet does not have. Every part here is SCOPED: the prose is compiled from markdown under content/, so its elements carry no classes and deliberately never will, because a class per element would put styling inside the content pipeline. It is also the block that forced `positions`: `:first-child` on the heading is not a state — nobody does it — it is where the rule sits, and the enum exists so that fact cannot grow into an arbitrary selector by increments.

block.title: Case study body
note: The prose of a case study: headings ruled off from each other, a measure on
the paragraphs, and the list marker the rest of the site uses.
IT USED TO BE `.case__content`, inside a full-screen modal that js/main.js
owned. The five case studies have pages at /work/<id> now and the modal is
gone, so what survives is the half that was never about being a modal — the
body itself. The name changed with the container: a class called
`__content` belongs to something, and this belongs to nothing but the prose.

rules.name: heading
rules.$doc: A section heading, ruled off above so the sections read as a stack of plates. <h3> because the page's <h1> is the project title and the section head above carries the number — the level is an outline decision, and changing it breaks the outline before it breaks anything visible.

rules.name: opening
rules.$doc: The first heading loses the rule and the space above it — a page does not open on a line. Three zeroes rather than a second set of values, because the declaration being undone is the one directly above.

rules.name: paragraph
rules.$doc: Body copy, held to a measure rather than to the well's full width. The measure is deliberate and narrower than the well: a case study is read, and the well is sized for an index that is scanned.

rules.name: emphasis
rules.$doc: Lifts to the primary ink; the prose around it sits at --content-body. A two-name element path, which is what the array form is for — the emitter supplies the combinator, so a descendant is the only relation an author can write.

rules.name: list
rules.$doc: The native marker off, so the drawn one below is the only one.

rules.name: item
rules.$doc: `position: relative` is here for the marker below it, which is absolutely positioned against this box; the left padding is the space that marker sits in.

declarations.aside: not surface-sunken: a surface token read as a border, which in dark sits behind the page and vanishes

rules.name: marker
rules.$doc: The list mark. Drawn with ::before rather than written into the text, so it is decoration and a screen reader does not read it out — which is the whole reason the content pipeline emits a plain <li>. Small and in the brand ink, so a list reads as a set of marks rather than as punctuation.

rules.name: item-emphasis
rules.$doc: The same lift inside a list item. Written twice rather than as one rule under two selectors, because that is what the stylesheet says and this is a transcription — the two are a paragraph apart and each belongs beside the element it qualifies.
